33296-five-young-men-messages-of-yesterd.creator: Charles Reynolds Brown
33296-five-young-men-messages-of-yesterd.description: A book by Charles Reynolds Brown. Here, for example, was a young man who was born on the sunny side of the street. He was the son of a rich man, and the favourite son. He was handsome--"It came to pass that Joseph was a goodly person and well favoured.

arxiv-2104-06153.title: The Impact of Activation Sparsity on Overfitting in Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2104-06153.creator: Karim Huesmann, Luis Garcia Rodriguez, Lars Linsen, Benjamin Risse ∗
arxiv-2104-06153.description: Abstract Overfitting is one of the fundamental challenges when training convolutional neural networks and is usually identified by a diverging training and test loss. The underlying dynamics of how the flow of activations induce overfitting is however poorly understood. In this study we introduce a perplexity-based sparsity definition to derive and visualise layer-wise activation measures.

arxiv-2108-01880.title: Theory of Huge Thermoelectric Effect Based on Magnon Drag Mechanism: Application to Thin-Film Heusler Alloy
arxiv-2108-01880.creator: Hiroyasu Matsuura, Masao Ogata, Takao Mori, Ernst Bauer
arxiv-2108-01880.description: Abstract To understand the unexpectedly high thermoelectric performance observed in the thin-film Heusler alloy Fe 2 V 0.8 W 0.2 Al, we study the magnon drag effect, generated by the tungsten based impurity band, as a possible source of this enhancement, in analogy to the phonon drag observed in FeSb 2 .

arxiv-2207-05637.title: Anomalous Cyclic in the Neutrino Oscillations
arxiv-2207-05637.creator: E. Aydiner
arxiv-2207-05637.description: Abstract Neutrino physics is one of the most important topics in particle physics and cosmology. Despite the many physical properties of neutrinos that are understood theoretically and experimentally, it is known that there are many unsolved problems in this area.

arxiv-2209-04298.title: Snowmass Neutrino Frontier: NF04 Topical Group Report Neutrinos from natural sources Submitted to the Proceedings of the US Community Study on the Future of Particle Physics (Snowmass 2021)
arxiv-2209-04298.creator: Y. Koshio, G.D. Orebi Gann, E. O’Sullivan, I. Tamborra
arxiv-2209-04298.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Y. Koshio, G.D. Orebi Gann, E. O’Sullivan, I. Tamborra. 1
Executive Summary

1.1
Physics of neutrinos from natural sources

This report covers a broad range of neutrino sources, from low-energy neutrinos from the early universe to ultra high-energy sources. We divide this report by source, and discuss the motivations for pursuing searches in each case, the current state of the field, and the prospects for future theoretical and experimental developments.

arxiv-2212-04548.title: STLGRU: Spatio-Temporal Lightweight Graph GRU for Traffic Flow Prediction
arxiv-2212-04548.creator: Kishor Kumar Bhaumik, Fahim Faisal Niloy, Simon S. Woo
arxiv-2212-04548.description: Abstract Reliable forecasting of traffic flow requires efficient modeling of traffic data. Indeed, different correlations and influences arise in a dynamic traffic network, making modeling a complicated task. Existing literature has proposed many different methods to capture traffic networks’ complex underlying spatial-temporal relations.

arxiv-2311-06654.title: Unsupervised and semi-supervised co-salient object detection via segmentation frequency statistics
arxiv-2311-06654.creator: Souradeep Chakraborty Shujon Naha Muhammet Bastan Amit Kumar K C Dimitris Samaras
arxiv-2311-06654.description: Abstract In this paper, we address the detection of co-occurring salient objects (CoSOD) in an image group using frequency statistics in an unsupervised manner, which further enable us to develop a semi-supervised method. While previous works have mostly focused on fully supervised CoSOD, less attention has been allocated to detecting co-salient objects when limited segmentation annotations are available for training.

arxiv-2404-02321.title: Exploring Substructure of the Near-Surface Shear Layer of the Sun Facilities: HMI(SDO), JSOC(Stanford and Lockheed)
arxiv-2404-02321.creator: M. Cristina Rabello Soares, Sarbani Basu, Richard S. Bogart
arxiv-2404-02321.description: Abstract The gradient of rotation in the near-surface shear layer (NSSL) of the Sun provides valuable insights into the dynamics associated with the solar activity cycle and the dynamo. Results obtained with global oscillation mode-splittings lack resolution near the surface, prompting the use of the local helioseismic ring-diagram method.

arxiv-2510-23577.title: TAMI: Taming Heterogeneity in Temporal Interactions for Temporal Graph Link Prediction
arxiv-2510-23577.creator: Zhongyi Yu, Jianqiu Wu, Zhenghao Wu, Shuhan Zhong, Weifeng Su, Chul-Ho Lee, Weipeng Zhuo
arxiv-2510-23577.description: Abstract Temporal graph link prediction aims to predict future interactions between nodes in a graph based on their historical interactions, which are encoded in node embeddings. We observe that heterogeneity naturally appears in temporal interactions, e.g., a few node pairs can make most interaction events, and interaction events happen at varying intervals.

arxiv-2601-02559.title: PerspectiveCoach : Exploring LLMs for Developer Reflection CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in HCI CCS: Human-centered computing Natural language interfaces CCS: Social and professional topics User characteristics CCS: Software and its engineering Software design engineering Conferenc
arxiv-2601-02559.creator: Lauren Olson, Emitzá Guzmán, Florian Kunneman
arxiv-2601-02559.description: Abstract . Despite growing awareness of ethical challenges in software development, practitioners still lack structured tools that help them critically engage with the lived experiences of marginalized users. This paper presents PerspectiveCoach , a large language model (LLM)-powered conversational tool designed to guide developers through structured perspective-taking exercises and deepen critical reflection on how software design decisions affect marginalized communities.

pmc-10697620.title: Atorvastatin for patients with cirrhosis. A randomized, placebo-controlled trial
pmc-10697620.creator: Thit M Kronborg, Robert Schierwagen, Kajetan Trošt, Qian Gao, Thomas Moritz, Flemming Bendtsen, Rasmus H Gantzel, Mette L Andersen, Ane S Teisner, Henning Grønbæk, Lise Hobolth, Søren Møller, Jonel Trebicka, Nina Kimer
pmc-10697620.description: Background:Patients with cirrhosis and portal hypertension face a high risk of complications. Besides their anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic effects, statins may reduce portal pressure and thus the risk of complications and mortality. We aimed to investigate the effects of atorvastatin on hospital admissions, mortality, inflammation, and lipidomics in cirrhosis with portal hypertension.

pmc-11348275.title: The importance of the location of the N-terminus in successful protein folding in vivo and in vitro
pmc-11348275.creator: Natalie R. Dall, Carolina A. T. F. Mendonça, Héctor L. Torres Vera, Susan Marqusee
pmc-11348275.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SignificanceProteins can fold cotranslationally, while still a ribosome nascent chain. This vectorial nature of protein synthesis can impact soluble, functional protein expression and interactions with proteostasis factors. To probe the importance of the N-terminus in this process, we generated all possible circular permutants (proteins with the same sequence and an altered start site) of a protein and monitored the changes in folding and soluble expression.

pmc-11494095.title: Modeling of railway track integrating a shock-absorbing mat at the sleepers-ballast interface using eigenfunctions of displacement
pmc-11494095.creator: C A Moubeke, Adoukatl Chanceu, R P Lemanlé Sanga, G E Ntamack, S Charif D’Ouazzane
pmc-11494095.description: Damage caused to railway tracks and the surrounding environment during trains passage have become a real concern for those involved in the railway sector over the years. To find a solution for this problem, several approaches have already been implemented on railway tracks in some countries.

pmc-11607196.title: The role of predominant polarity on cognitive dysfunctions in patients with bipolar disorder
pmc-11607196.creator: Ekin Atay, Çağatay Ermiş, İrem Nur Gökbayrak Atay, Ömer Aydemir, Erol Özmen
pmc-11607196.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundCognitive impairment is frequently observed in bipolar disorder (BD). Previous findings indicated that predominant polarity could have an effect on cognitive deficits. This study aimed to examine the association between predominant polarity and cognitive impairments in BD.Materials and methodsEuthymic BD patients with manic (MPP, n = 31), depressive (DPP, n = 25), undetermined predominant polarity (UPP, n = 28), and healthy controls (HC, n = 27) participated in the study. A battery of neurocognitive and social cognitive tests was implemented.

pmc-13130360.title: Structural brain variability in recent-onset and chronic schizophrenia: evidence from person-based similarity index analysis
pmc-13130360.creator: Young Tak Jo, Jungsun Lee, Sun Min Kim, Hyeongyu Park, Sung Woo Joo
pmc-13130360.description: Objective:Structural abnormalities in cortical and subcortical brain regions are consistently observed in schizophrenia; however, substantial inter-individual variability complicates identifying clear neurobiological biomarkers. The Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI) quantifies individual structural variability; however, its applicability across schizophrenia stages remains unclear. This study aimed to compare cortical and subcortical structural variability in recent-onset and chronic schizophrenia and explore associations with clinical measures.

pmc-13137206.title: Increased frequency of remote and off-site work impacts incident learning workflows in radiation oncology
pmc-13137206.creator: Ethan Steele, Matthew Whitmill, Ross McGurk, Xianming Tan, Alison Amos, Zachary Oaks, Michael Dance, Ashley Weiner, Lukasz Mazur, Lawrence B. Marks, Bhishamjit Chera, Shivani Sud
pmc-13137206.description: Highlights•Recent events have led to shifts in culture in favor of increased remote work.•Workflows in radiation oncology have adapted to facilitate remote work.•Changed workflows are associated with changes in event reporting.•Communication is frequently cited as a contributor to reported incidents.•Event severity has not increased despite these changed workflows.

pmc-13624131.creator: Cui-Ping Zhang, Zhi-Yong Wang, Xue-Wei Wang, Zhi Li
pmc-13624131.description: As a common greenhouse-grown commercial crop, chili pepper yields have always been a focus of attention. Effective management is essential for both environmental sustainability and high productivity in greenhouses. Whether for growth monitoring, yield estimates, and automated production, precise identification of chili flowers is critical.
